title: BCCI Anti-Corruption Unit Puts State T20 League Stakeholders Under Scanner
excerpt: Bookies, players, and franchise owners face heightened scrutiny as the proliferation of domestic T20 tournaments creates new vulnerabilities for match-fixing.
body:
• The BCCI's Anti-Corruption Unit has intensified its scrutiny of state-level T20 leagues, with bookies, players, and team owners coming under the scanner.
  • Multiple state T20 tournaments — including leagues in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Uttar Pradesh — have faced corruption probes in recent seasons.
  • The BCCI issued a stern seven-page advisory to IPL franchises during the 2026 season, warning of "misconduct and protocol violations" by players, staff, and owners.
  • The crackdown reflects growing concern that the proliferation of domestic T20 franchises has created new vulnerabilities for match-fixing and illegal betting.

State Leagues in the Spotlight

The Board of Control for Cricket in India's Anti-Corruption Unit has placed bookies, players, and franchise owners of state-level T20 leagues under heightened scrutiny as the mushrooming of domestic franchise cricket creates new avenues for corruption, according to reports from multiple cricket outlets.

The intensified investigation comes after a string of corruption incidents across state T20 tournaments in recent years that have exposed the vulnerability of domestic cricket to match-fixing and illegal betting networks. The Karnataka Premier League, Tamil Nadu Premier League, and Uttar Pradesh T20 League have all faced probes that led to player arrests, FIRs, and suspensions.

The ACU's expanded mandate reflects what BCCI officials have acknowledged is a systemic challenge: as India's cricket ecosystem expands beyond the Indian Premier League into dozens of state-level and city-level T20 franchise tournaments, the anti-corruption infrastructure has struggled to keep pace.

"In some of the states it has gone to the next level. We are dealing with it and have to get the anti-corruption system right. Nobody wants this — it doesn't help anyone."

— BCCI official on state T20 league corruption

A Growing List of Incidents

The Karnataka Premier League was suspended after police investigations led to the arrests of several players, including India international Abhimanyu Mithun, on charges related to spot-fixing. The scandal rocked domestic cricket and prompted the BCCI to order a comprehensive review of the league's operations.

In Tamil Nadu, the BCCI's ACU probed links between players and bookies in the Tamil Nadu Premier League. The ACU's then-head, Ajit Singh, told ESPNCricinfo that the inquiry focused on identifying who had made corrupt approaches to players. "The players have told us we have received these messages, so it is not an inquiry against the player. There were messages seeking match-related information. We presume it's coming from those who are interested in betting," Singh said.

In Uttar Pradesh, the Lucknow police filed an FIR following a complaint from the BCCI's ACU about an attempted fix during the UP T20 League in 2025. A bookie reportedly offered Rs 1 crore to a team manager to influence match results, promising Rs 50 lakh in commission. The team manager reported the approach, and ACU officers conducted a sting operation that led to charges under multiple criminal statutes, according to CricTracker.

IPL Also Under Watch

The corruption concerns extend beyond state leagues to the IPL itself. During the 2026 IPL season, the BCCI issued a stern seven-page advisory to all franchises after the Anti-Corruption and Security Unit flagged "certain anomalies" involving unauthorized personnel in team areas, according to Wisden.

"The Anti-Corruption and Security Unit has flagged certain anomalies and submitted a report about unauthorised persons being seen in the dugout, team bus and team hotel during IPL matches," IPL chairman Arun Dhumal told PTI. The BCCI also noted franchise owners attempting to communicate with players during live match situations — conduct that "directly contravenes established protocol," according to the advisory.

BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia warned that the incidents, "if left unaddressed, carry the potential to cause significant reputational harm to the tournament, the franchise concerned, and the BCCI as the governing body."

Strengthening the System

The BCCI has taken several steps to strengthen its anti-corruption capabilities. The board partnered with Sportradar, a global sports integrity firm, to monitor betting patterns during IPL matches using its Fraud Detection System, which tracks odds movements across more than 600 bookmakers worldwide. The BCCI also established an Intelligence Gathering Unit in collaboration with Maharashtra Police to proactively gather intelligence on corruption-related activities in cricket.

The challenges, however, remain formidable. With state T20 leagues operating under varying levels of oversight and franchise owners in some tournaments lacking transparent backgrounds, the BCCI's anti-corruption officials have flagged concerns about the "identity of the owners of certain domestic franchises and lack of a transparent process around how those franchises had been awarded," according to ICC meeting minutes reviewed by media outlets.

As Indian cricket continues its rapid commercial expansion, the integrity of its newest tournaments will depend on whether the BCCI's anti-corruption machinery can keep pace with the scale and speed of franchise cricket's growth across the country.
